q: Where should the ask appear in an email that gets answered?
options: In the final paragraph, after full background
In the first two lines
Only in the subject line
In a separate follow-up email
explanation: Busy readers decide within seconds whether to keep reading. State what you want in the first two lines; background comes after.

q: What is the rule about email purpose?
options: One email, one purpose — three asks in one email get one thing or nothing
Pack as many requests as possible into each email
Never state a purpose directly
Send a separate email for every sentence
explanation: One email, one purpose. Multiple asks dilute attention and make it easy for the reader to answer none of them.

q: The 8-post month pack is built from:
options: Eight copied posts from other pages
One real business story turned into 2 offers, 2 proof, 2 tips, 2 behind-the-scenes
Eight different businesses
Whatever the AI invents about your industry
explanation: One real story feeds all eight posts — offers, proof, tips, behind-the-scenes — which keeps the month's content truthful and consistent.

q: How does the lesson describe turning these skills into a service?
options: As a guaranteed income if you follow the steps
As a get-rich scheme requiring many clients immediately
As how to offer it — a monthly arrangement with one or two businesses — with no income promise
As something only agency staff can do
explanation: The course describes honestly how to offer the service and refuses to promise income. Whether anyone pays depends on your market, quality and follow-through.

q: Which customer message structure closes orders with less back-and-forth?
options: Long friendly chats where price is negotiated fresh each time
A clear message: item, price, what's included, delivery date, how to order
Replying only when the customer messages three times
Withholding the price until the customer visits
explanation: Chidinma is an illustrative composite, not a documented customer case. Clear price and delivery messages make terms easier to understand; improved orders or time savings have not been measured.
